title: Module restriction on a specified twisted site
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site with pullbacks, let $s:C\simeq C$ have both directions continuous, let $R$ be a commutative ring sheaf, and let $a:(s^{-1})^*R\simeq R$. Use the Site, module translation $\sigma$, and fixed-pair definitions of [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data]. For every specified $S:\operatorname{Site}(J,s,R,a)$ there are an equivalence $e:\operatorname{Mod}(S.\mathrm{coefficient})\simeq\operatorname{Pairs}(\sigma)$ and a natural isomorphism from $e$ followed by forgetting to ordinary restriction with scalars transported by $S.\mathrm{coefficientRestriction}^{-1}$. For every module and every base object, this isomorphism identifies restriction along the minus-one generator with the inverse of its fixed-pair structure, exactly as in RestrictionPresentation.module_generator. No set presentation, geometric morphism, or translation-equivalence data is asserted.

source.place: Original twisted-site steps 3 and 4; Tag 00W0 motivation (proposition-sheaves-on-group); Stacks Modules on Sites 03CV.

proof.text: Construct the minus-one natural isomorphism from s.inverse followed by inclusion to inclusion. The category identity equations force powerComp(-1,0) and powerComp(0,-1) to be identities. A degree-one arrow built from the counit has invertible degree-zero composites with the generator, hence the generator is invertible. The arrow composition equations give its naturality.

Use coefficient_generator to identify the two coefficient maps under that natural isomorphism. Apply SheafOfModules.pushforwardCongr₂ and pushforwardComp to obtain a natural isomorphism U ≅ U followed by sigma. Its inverse supplies the fixed-pair structure. Naturality constructs the functor on morphisms, with identity and composition inherited from U. The inverse identity gives the displayed generator normalization. Restriction is faithful because every copied object is inclusion X.

For a morphism of the constructed fixed pairs, cancel their invertible structure maps to get commutation with generator restriction. Apply the module morphism extension theorem. Faithfulness shows uniqueness, giving fullness.

Apply individual object extension to a fixed pair, producing a coefficient module sheaf and the base restriction isomorphism. Its generator equation, after canceling the invertible generator restriction, proves that the isomorphism intertwines the structure maps. This gives essential surjectivity. Combine full, faithful, and essentially surjective using Functor.asEquivalence. Forgetting the pair is definitionally U, so the natural restriction comparison is the identity, and the proved generator normalization gives the required equation.

proof_origin.place: Original twisted variant of 00W0, steps 3 and 4; explicit forward functor, separated object and morphism extension.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleRestriction [HasPullbacks C] (S : Site J s R a) :
    letI := S.category
    letI := S.inclusion_continuous
    ∃ (e : Modules S.coefficient ≌ Pairs (sigma J s R a))
      (c : e.functor ⋙ forgetPairs (sigma J s R a) ≅
        SheafOfModules.pushforward
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map S.coefficientRestriction.inv)),
      (∀ (M : Modules S.coefficient) (X : C)
        (x : ((sigma J s R a).obj (e.functor.obj M).obj.a).val.obj (op X)),
        (c.hom.app M).val.app (op (s.inverse.obj X)) x =
          M.val.map ((S.arrows (s.inverse.obj X) X).symm ⟨-1, 𝟙 _⟩).op
            ((c.hom.app M).val.app (op X)
              ((e.functor.obj M).obj.str.val.app (op X) x)))
